key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving electronic uniformity, showing that morphology and optoelectronic quality can be decoupled.
engineering_relevance: Mixed-dimensional capping offers a route to more durable perovskite photovoltaics without requiring smoother surfaces.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Compare statistical AFM topography with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence and quasi-Fermi level splitting.
Evaluate pristine and capped films under accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and better-preserved optoelectronic homogeneity during aging.
watch_item: The abstract does not report device-efficiency gains or aging conditions, limiting assessment of practical photovoltaic durability.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
